title: Light-time iteration and body-specific apparent position paths
description:
Implement body-specific pre-processing that runs before app_pos_rest, in src/calc.rs.

## 1. Light-time iteration (sweph.c:2545–2596)

Newton iteration for retarded position: t' = t − |Δx|/c.
- **Moshier backend**: 0 iterations. Uses linear extrapolation: apparent = true − (light_time × velocity). Still computes light-time for the distance correction.
- **File backends** (future): 1–2 iterations with re-evaluation at retarded time.
- Speed correction: 3-point difference to get d(dt)/dt, apparent_speed = true_speed × (1 − d(dt)/dt).
- Light-time = |planet − observer| × AUNIT / CLIGHT / 86400 (days).

## 2. `app_pos_etc_plan()` (sweph.c:2465–2776) — planets

For Mercury through Pluto:
1. Apply ICRS→J2000 frame bias (if not ICRS flag) — calls `bias::frame_bias()`
2. Light-time iteration (step 1 above)
3. Delegate to `app_pos_rest()` for aberration→deflection→precession→nutation→ecliptic→polar→units

Needs Earth heliocentric position as input (for aberration/deflection geometry).

## 3. `app_pos_etc_sun()` (sweph.c:~2350–2464) — Sun

Sun is special:
- Geocentric Sun = −(Earth barycentric), already computed by Moshier backend
- Light-time: constant ~8.3 minutes (compute from distance, don't iterate)
- Still applies aberration and deflection unless suppressed
- Planet heliocentric position for deflection = zeros (Sun IS the deflecting body for others, but for the Sun itself, different handling — extract details from c-ref-calc.md)

## 4. `app_pos_etc_moon()` (sweph.c:~2200–2350) — Moon

Moon is special:
- No light-time iteration (negligible at 1.3 light-seconds)
- No gravitational deflection (Moon is too close, deflection formula doesn't apply)
- Aberration: still applied, but Earth velocity used directly
- Speed: already computed via central differences in Moshier backend

## Architecture note

These functions take the raw output from `moshier::backend::compute()` (geocentric equatorial J2000 [x,y,z,vx,vy,vz]) and produce corrected coordinates. They are the bridge between backend → output.

Each function also needs access to:
- Earth heliocentric position (from Moshier backend with body=Sun, negated)
- Obliquity at J2000 and at date
- Nutation at date
- AstroModels for precession/nutation model selection

C source reference: docs/c-ref-calc.md

acceptance_criteria.text: Light-time iteration implemented (0-iteration Moshier path, extensible for file backends)
Golden tests: planets at multiple epochs through full correction pipeline
Test TRUEPOS vs default to verify corrections are applied correctly
Light-time correction magnitude is physically reasonable (~8min Sun, varies for planets)

execution_record: Scope was fully implemented under swisseph-rs/30 (commit c6e9d27) and swisseph-rs/34 (commit d801e48 FP fidelity fixes). calc_planet, calc_sun, calc_moon all implemented in src/calc.rs with light-time iteration (0-iter Moshier path), deflection, aberration, frame bias, precession, and nutation. 350-case golden test suite (7 bodies × 5 epochs × 10 flag combos) passes with 1e-10 tolerance. Moon correctly skips deflection. No additional work required.
